summary: Rabies human monoclonal antibody (e.g., Rabishield, manufactured by Serum Institute of India) is a recombinant human monoclonal antibody that provides the passive-immunization component of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) for individuals with suspected rabies exposure (notably WHO Category III exposures). It substitutes for rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). The dose is 3.33 IU/kg body weight, infiltrated as fully as anatomically feasible into and around the wound(s), with any remaining volume given intramuscularly at a site distant from the vaccine. It must be combined with a full course of rabies vaccine, given at the time of the first vaccine dose (and may be given up to day 7 of the vaccine series). It is not FDA-approved; it is licensed in India, was the first rabies monoclonal antibody approved worldwide, and has been on the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines since 2021. It neutralizes rabies virus by binding the viral glycoprotein.
indications: Passive immunization (antibody) component of rabies post-exposure prophylaxis in individuals with suspected rabies exposure (e.g., WHO Category III exposures), given together with a full rabies vaccine course

dosage.d: 3.33 IU/kg body weight as a single dose
dosage.t: Single administration (with the first rabies vaccine dose)
dosage.n: Infiltrate into and around the wound(s); inject any remaining volume IM at a site distant from the vaccine

admin: Administer as soon as possible after exposure, preferably at the time of the first rabies vaccine dose (may be given up to day 7 of the vaccine series)
If anatomically feasible, thoroughly infiltrate the full calculated dose into and around the wound(s)
Inject any remaining volume intramuscularly at a site distant from where the rabies vaccine is given
Do NOT use the same syringe or injection site as the rabies vaccine, and do not exceed the calculated dose (excess antibody can suppress active vaccine response)
Always accompany with thorough wound washing and a complete rabies vaccination course
moa: Rabies human monoclonal antibody is a recombinant human antibody that binds a conserved epitope on the rabies virus surface glycoprotein, neutralizing the virus at and around the wound. This passive immunization provides immediate, ready-made neutralizing antibody to control virus at the inoculation site during the interval before the patient's own active immune response to rabies vaccine develops.

absolute: Known severe hypersensitivity to the product or its components (rabies PEP itself is essentially never withheld after a genuine exposure given the near-universal fatality of rabies)
relative: Prior receipt of a rabies vaccine series with documented adequate immunity (passive antibody generally not needed)
monitor: Completion and timing of the full rabies vaccine course
Wound healing and signs of secondary infection

preg: Rabies is almost universally fatal once symptomatic, so post-exposure prophylaxis - including the antibody component - is considered life-saving and is not contraindicated in pregnancy. Pregnancy should not delay or prevent appropriate rabies PEP.
lact: Breastfeeding is not a contraindication to rabies post-exposure prophylaxis; the monoclonal antibody and rabies vaccine should be given as indicated, and nursing may continue.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is described; the product is given once as wound infiltration plus IM injection of any remainder, with weight-based dosing only.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is described; dosing is weight-based and administered as a single wound infiltration with IM remainder.

major: Excess dose of passive antibody (above 3.33 IU/kg) can interfere with the active immune response to rabies vaccine - do not exceed the calculated dose
moderate: Do not mix or co-inject with rabies vaccine; use separate syringes and distant sites to avoid neutralizing vaccine antigen
minor: Live attenuated vaccines - general caution applies, though rabies PEP takes priority

common: Injection/infiltration site pain, swelling, or redness
emergency: Anaphylaxis or severe allergic reaction at the time of administration

monitoring: Local reaction at the wound infiltration and IM injection sites
Adherence to and completion of the full rabies vaccine schedule

counsel: This injection gives immediate antibody protection at the bite wound while the rabies vaccine builds your own immunity
It is essential to complete the entire rabies vaccine course on schedule - the antibody alone is not sufficient
Keep the wound clean; report increasing redness, swelling, pus, or fever
Tell the staff right away about any rash, itching, swelling, or trouble breathing after the injection
Do not miss any scheduled vaccine doses
pk: Provides immediate passive neutralizing antibody at and around the wound
Antibody is present locally on administration; systemic distribution follows the IM remainder
Long elimination half-life typical of IgG monoclonal antibodies (weeks)
Bridges protection until the active vaccine response develops (about 1-2 weeks)
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light (per manufacturer)
pearls: Biologic (recombinant human monoclonal antibody) used as the passive component of rabies PEP - a modern substitute for rabies immunoglobulin (RIG)

Dose is 3.33 IU/kg, infiltrated into/around the wound; give any remainder IM distant from the vaccine - never co-inject with the vaccine and never exceed the calculated dose (can suppress vaccine response)
Must always be paired with a full rabies vaccine course; can be given up to day 7 of the vaccine series
NOT FDA-approved; licensed in India (Rabishield, Serum Institute), the first rabies monoclonal antibody approved worldwide, and on the WHO Essential Medicines List since 2021
Neutralizes rabies virus by binding the viral glycoprotein; PEP is not withheld in pregnancy or lactation
missed: Not applicable in the conventional sense - the antibody is a single PEP dose given as early as possible (up to day 7 of the vaccine course). The accompanying rabies vaccine doses must not be missed; if a vaccine dose is delayed, contact the clinic to resume the schedule promptly.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with weight-based single dosing. Exceeding the recommended 3.33 IU/kg does not improve outcomes and may suppress the active immune response to the rabies vaccine; therefore the calculated dose should not be exceeded. Management of any reaction is supportive.
